# A3. Debits and Credits {#sec-dr-cr .appendix}

Start with the economic event and its effects on assets, liabilities, and equity. Debit and credit notation records those effects; it does not determine whether the event should be recognized.

## Account directions

| Account type | Increase | Decrease | Usual balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Asset | Debit | Credit | Debit |
| Liability | Credit | Debit | Credit |
| Contributed equity | Credit | Debit | Credit |
| Retained earnings | Credit | Debit | Credit; a deficit can be a debit |
| Revenue | Credit | Debit | Credit before closing |
| Expense | Debit | Credit | Debit before closing |
| Distributions to owners | Debit | Credit | Debit before closing |
| Accumulated depreciation (contra-asset) | Credit | Debit | Credit |

Revenue and expense accounts record the period's performance. At closing their net effect is transferred to retained earnings. Distributions reduce equity but are not expenses. Cash is one asset account; a debit does not always mean cash received.

## Three entries from Campus Curb

| Event | Debit | Credit | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Insurance coverage used | Insurance expense 1,000 | Prepaid insurance 1,000 | A previously paid benefit has been consumed. |
| Subscription service provided | Unearned revenue 1,250 | Service revenue 1,250 | Part of the service obligation has been satisfied. |
| Interest accumulated | Interest expense 50 | Interest payable 50 | A contractual obligation has accumulated without payment. |

[The complete FSET example](a01-fset.qmd) maps every transaction and adjustment to entries and the adjusted trial balance.

## What equal debits and credits prove

Equal totals establish a form of internal consistency. They do not prove that a reported receivable exists, that an estimate is appropriate, or that all obligations were recorded. A fictitious receivable and revenue can balance. Evidence and controls address questions the bookkeeping identity cannot answer.
